## The rule

A credential or permission blocker is **owner-gated only after `sudo -n` has also failed.** On this dev box the agent user has `NOPASSWD: ALL`, so the Postgres superuser is always one command away:

```bash
sudo -n -u postgres psql -d papercusp -c '<SQL>'
```

When you do escalate, name the privileged paths you actually tried. *"No superuser is reachable"* is a claim about **your probe set**, not about the machine — and stating it the second way converts a five-second fix into the owner's problem.

## The worked example (P-037 / WI-40505, 2026-08-27)

The hosted auth lane needed exactly one statement:

```sql
GRANT hosted_app TO harness_app WITH INHERIT FALSE;
```

The agent established the hard parts correctly — `harness_admin` is not superuser, holds no ADMIN OPTION on `hosted_app`, and Postgres refuses the grant with *"Only roles with the ADMIN option on role hosted_app may grant this role"*. It then probed password auth, peer auth, `~/.pgpass` and the environment, found nothing, and filed an owner-gated wall.

It never tried `sudo`. The owner's reply was *"you can get super user access"* and *"other agents do this all the time"* — so this is a recurring class, not a one-off.

What makes it seductive: **every individual finding was correct and verified.** The reasoning was sound right up to the conclusion, which quietly substituted "I could not find a way" for "there is no way". A well-evidenced wall is still a wall in the wrong place.

## The technical invariant underneath it

Worth knowing on its own, because no single file states it and it spans three that never reference each other:

| file | states | omits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `978-hosted-customer-rls.sql` | creates `hosted_app` `NOLOGIN NOINHERIT`; grants every RLS policy `TO hosted_app` | that something must be a *member* of it |
| `connection.ts` | the pool connects as `harness_app` | that `harness_app` is REVOKED from the hosted tables |
| `tenant-context.ts` | installs the `app.*` GUCs | that GUCs alone do nothing without the role switch |

So:

1. `hosted_app` is **assume-only**. It is `NOLOGIN` and 978 re-verifies that on every run, so a separate "hosted pool" is architecturally impossible — not merely discouraged. The hosted path must `SET LOCAL ROLE hosted_app` from the ordinary pool connection.
2. That requires membership, which no migration granted. Migration **997** adds it.
3. `WITH INHERIT FALSE` is **load-bearing, not style**: `harness_app` has `rolinherit = true`, so a default membership hands *every ordinary query* ambient hosted privileges with no `SET ROLE` anywhere — dissolving the exact FORCE RLS boundary 978 exists to build.
4. A missing grant fails **closed** (`permission denied for table`), never open. Worth stating plainly, because the gap first reads like a live cross-tenant leak and is not one.

### Verifying it, as the real pool role

```bash
PGPASSWORD=harness_app_pwd psql "postgresql://harness_app@localhost:5432/papercusp"
#   SELECT count(*) FROM papercusp_auth.hosted_users;   -> permission denied   (no ambient privileges)
#   BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE hosted_app; ...               -> succeeds, RLS applies
#   COMMIT; then the same SELECT                        -> denied again        (pooled conn cannot retain it)
```

All three must hold. The first is what `WITH INHERIT FALSE` buys you; the third is what `SET LOCAL` (rather than `SET`) buys you.

## Testing note that cost a cycle

Migration 997's raise-branch is unreachable when the migration user *can* grant — it repairs the unsafe membership before the post-condition reads it. A falsifiability probe run as `postgres` therefore reports "guard did not fire" and looks like a broken guard. Simulate the under-privileged path instead:

```sql
BEGIN;
GRANT hosted_app TO harness_app WITH INHERIT TRUE;  -- the unsafe state
SET LOCAL ROLE harness_admin;                       -- now can_grant = false
\i libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/997-hosted-app-role-membership.sql
ROLLBACK;
```

That raises, and the same instrument passes against the safe state as a positive control. The general point: when a guard both **repairs** and **checks**, a probe run with repair privileges measures the repair, not the check.

Related: plan decision `D-138`, and the `CLAUDE.md` invariant `a-blocker-is-work-not-a-stop-exhaust-sudo-first`.
